vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-129509 - Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider: S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator disables S3 TLS verification by default
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129509
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 9:37 a.m. | 1 hour, 1 minute ago
  
Description :In the Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider 10.2.0 through 15.3.0, `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` turned off TLS certificate verification for its connection to Amazon S3 by default (`s3_verify=False`), whatever the AWS connection's own verification settings were. An attacker positioned on the network between an Airflow worker and S3 could intercept that traffic, read the signed requests and alter the listed object keys and the copied file contents. Deployments are affected when a Dag uses `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` without setting `s3_verify`. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-microsoft-azure 15.3.1 or later, which uses the AWS connection's verification settings by default.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99316 - ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99316
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 5 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and
only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb,
sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs
of each direction.

A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so
the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run
before those pointers are set.  While the stream is still being
synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls
playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still
NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7]
  RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33
  Call Trace:
   
   stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596
   i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654
   __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657
   usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691
   tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994
   handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645
   

The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and
do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit
loop.  Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a
well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills
and resubmits the streams.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99312 - KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99312
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 5 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-110307 - Incorrect authorization vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed unauthorized control of enterprise-owned GitHub Apps via user and enterprise ID collision
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-110307
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 2:17 a.m. | 16 minutes ago
  
Description :An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated user whose numeric user ID matched an enterprise's numeric ID to manage that enterprise's GitHub Apps and generate private keys without enterprise membership. GitHub App ownership checks compared numeric IDs without checking the owner's account type. Exploitation required control of a session for the colliding user account and an enterprise-owned GitHub App. A generated private key could be used to authenticate as the App and access repositories where it was installed, within its granted permissions. On standard fresh installations, the documented collision involved the non-loginable built-in ghost account; the reported GHES reproduction used site administrator impersonation. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.
  
Severity: 7.4 | HIGH

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-129892 - IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129892
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 11:39 p.m. | 39 minutes ago
  
Description :IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source.

The rewrite copies the module's source down to the built-in list's heredoc and appends each fetched line below it. Nothing checks that a line looks like a domain. A line that is not a comment loses only what follows a `//` and its trailing whitespace, so a line reading END_BUILTIN_DATA is appended as it stands and ends the data block in the rewritten file. Every fetched line after it is Perl.

Arbitrary Perl runs in every process that loads IO::Socket::SSL, which loads this module unconditionally, until the file is reinstalled. The attacker must control the fetched list, through the cleartext default URL or a caller-supplied one, and the updater must run with write access to the installed module.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-121757 - CP949 decoder may read past input
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-121757
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 10:23 p.m. | 10 minutes ago
  
Description :Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If //IGNORE is set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on the destination of the conversion and the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-95822 - Out-of-bounds read and kernel stack disclosure in the SOCKS5 client when the destination address family differs from the proxy address family
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-95822
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 8:17 p.m. | 24 minutes ago
  
Description :The SOCKS5 client in subsys/net/lib/socks/socks.c built the CONNECT request in socks5_tcp_connect() by choosing the SOCKS5 address type from the address family of the proxy (proxy->sa_family) while reading the bytes out of the destination address supplied to connect(). A SOCKS5 request encodes the destination independently of the transport used to reach the proxy, so the two families are unrelated and nothing in the path forces them to agree: set_context_proxy() only requires the proxy family to match the socket, and zsock_connect_ctx() enters the SOCKS branch before any destination validation. With an IPv6 proxy and an AF_INET destination the code treated an 8-byte struct net_sockaddr_in as a struct net_sockaddr_in6 and copied the 16-byte sin6_addr from it, reading 12 bytes past the end of the object and transmitting them to the proxy.

With CONFIG_USERSPACE enabled, z_vrfy_zsock_connect() copies only addrlen user bytes into a stack-resident struct net_sockaddr_storage and enforces no per-family minimum length, so the oversized read stays within the storage but returns stale, uninitialised kernel-stack bytes. An unprivileged user-mode thread can therefore open an AF_INET6 stream socket, point setsockopt(SO_SOCKS5) at a proxy it controls, and call connect() with a short AF_INET destination to have the kernel send it 12 bytes of supervisor stack residue per attempt. Without CONFIG_USERSPACE the read runs past the end of the caller's own struct net_sockaddr_in, disclosing adjacent memory to the proxy; the family mismatch can arise unintentionally when a destination is obtained from DNS while an IPv6 proxy is configured.

Impact is limited to information disclosure of at most 12 bytes per connect() call, with no write primitive; the leak is delivered to whoever operates the SOCKS5 proxy. The mirrored pairing (IPv6 destination through an IPv4 proxy) is memory-safe but encoded the destination as SOCKS5_ATYP_IPV4 from the first four bytes of the IPv6 address, causing the proxy to connect to an unrelated host. Exploitation requires the non-default CONFIG_SOCKS option, a socket with SO_SOCKS5 configured, and both IPv4 and IPv6 support in the image.

The fix moves the encoding into a helper that selects the address type from dest->sa_family and validates dest_len against the matching struct net_sockaddr_in/struct net_sockaddr_in6 before copying, rejecting under-length or unsupported destinations with an error.
  
Severity: 3.3 | LOW
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

Without CONFIG_USERSPACE the read runs past the end of the caller's own struct net_sockaddr_in, disclosing adjacent memory to the proxy; the family mismatch can arise unintentionally when a destination is obtained from DNS while an IPv6 proxy is configured.

Impact is limited to information disclosure of at most 12 bytes per connect() call, with no write primitive; the leak is delivered to whoever operates the SOCKS5 proxy. The mirrored pairing (IPv6 destination through an IPv4 proxy) is memory-safe but encoded the destination as SOCKS5_ATYP_IPV4 from the first four bytes of the IPv6 address, causing the proxy to connect to an unrelated host. Exploitation requires the non-default CONFIG_SOCKS option, a socket with SO_SOCKS5 configured, and both IPv4 and IPv6 support in the image.

The fix moves the encoding into a helper that selects the address type from dest->sa_family and validates dest_len against the matching struct net_sockaddr_in/struct net_sockaddr_in6 before copying, rejecting under-length or unsupported destinations with an error.
  
Severity: 3.3 | LOW

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-86061 - Teable: child-resource lookups permit cross-tenant data access and modification
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-86061
  
Published : 17 novembre 2026 17:53 | 26 minutes ago
  
Description :Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264, the routes for PluginService::regenerateSecret and PluginService::delete carry no @Permissions decorator, and the methods omit plugin ownership checks. An authenticated attacker can directly target another plugin's identifier to rotate and disclose its OAuth secret or delete the plugin, including system plugins. Separately, PermissionGuard authorizes several nested API requests using a caller-controlled parent tableId, baseId, or spaceId, while the services resolve the requested child object only by its globally unique identifier. An authenticated attacker can provide a parent resource the attacker owns together with a victim's child identifier. ViewService::getViewById can then disclose another tenant's view configuration, embedded filter values, field layout, and shareId. DashboardService::updatePluginStorage and the view-position updatePluginStorage path can overwrite another tenant's plugin storage because the plugin installation is not rebound to the authorized base, dashboard, table, or view. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-130627 - Vert.x HTTP client forwards Authorization and all headers to cross-authority redirect target when followRedirects(true)
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-130627
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 2:21 p.m. | 10 minutes ago
  
Description :The Vert.x HTTP client transport (a2a-java-sdk-http-client-vertx) hand-rolls a POST redirect follower that, when the documented PostBuilder.followRedirects(true) opt-in is enabled, re-issues the redirected request with the full request header map copied verbatim and performs no credential stripping and no same-authority check. A malicious, compromised, or mistyped agent that returns a 30x response with an absolute cross-host Location causes the client to forward the standard Authorization header (Bearer/Basic/OAuth) — plus every other header, including the allowlisted API-key headers — to the attacker-controlled authority. This breaks the project's own cross-transport invariant (SECURITY.md §8, OkHttpPostRedirectHeaderLeakTest) that credentials are stripped on cross-authority redirects even when redirects are followed. The sibling JDK and OkHttp/Android transports strip Authorization; Vert.x uniquely does not. This is a "fix introduced the bug" variant — the follower was added by the GHSA-9rhm hardening PR (3ae82912, refined by a5e76a0b).

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-127138 - Circumvention of offline barcode revocation check in pretixSCAN
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-127138
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 12:09 p.m. | 1 hour, 6 minutes ago
  
Description :pretix provides a mechanism where ticket QR codes are cryptographically signed and can be verified by our pretixSCAN apps in offline mode without any database of valid tickets. pretixSCAN checks the signature to verify that the ticket was issued by the correct pretix event and compares the QR code against a list of revoked QR codes. A QR code becomes revoked when the order is canceled, or the ticket is changed in a way that a new QR code needs to be generated.




However, the parsing of the QR code in all of our pretixSCAN apps contained a faulty computation, rendering the check for the correct length of the contents faulty. This way, an attacker is able to craft multiple QR codes for the same ticket which have the same content, but look different and therefore do not match against the revocation list. This does not allow to fabricate entirely new tickets, but it does allow to enter the event with e.g. a canceled ticket. This attack requires pretixSCAN to be scanning in offline mode and the "pretix signature scheme 1" to be used for the event's QR codes.




If the attack is executed, the ticket unfortunately shows as valid (green) on the scanner but as invalid (red) on the server since the server later cannot match it to a ticket. We scanned the entire database of scans on pretix Hosted and could not find any traces of this being exploited in the past.
  
Severity: 6.8 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: Critical Java Vulnerability Requires Immediate Patching
vulnerability.summary:
Purpose
CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed Oracle Java vulnerability CVE-2026-114938. This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as “Java4Shell,” affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK). Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution.
Actions to take
CISA urges organizations to take the following actions:

Identify affected Java installations. Review your software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, including those bundled with third-party applications or included in container images and appliances. Note: JDKs and Java runtimes may not appear as separate entries in software inventories.
Apply relevant Java and vendor patches as soon as they are available, prioritizing internet-facing systems.

If immediate patching is not feasible, implement temporary compensating controls, such as restricting and validating Base64 input at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits, and limiting unauthenticated access.


Review Oracle’s security advisory for guidance on patching and affected products and versions.
 Monitor for indicators of suspicious activity, including rogue runtimes, unexpected JVM crashes, and suspicious Java processes.

Resources
CISA urges network defenders to review the following resource and apply necessary updates:
Vendor Guidance

Oracle’s Security Advisory: Critical Security Patch Update – November 2026

vulnerability.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
vulnerability.summary:
CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

CVE-2026-115731 Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise.
Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.
While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.
Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-125163 - TYPO3 CMS - Unrestricted File Upload in Form Framework
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-125163
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 11:17 a.m. | 42 minutes ago
  
Description :The FileUpload and ImageUpload elements of the Form Framework use the property allowedMimeTypes as an allow list of MIME types accepted for upload. An empty allowedMimeTypes list was treated as "no restriction". Forms containing upload elements without any configured MIME type, for example in manually created form definitions or when all MIME types were deselected in the form editor, accepted any file except those blocked by the file deny pattern, which only covers PHP-related file extensions. This allowed unauthenticated users to upload files with browser-executable content, such as HTML or SVG documents, to the configured upload folder, which by default is located in a public storage. If attackers know the URL of an uploaded file (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-029), this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder.
  
Severity: 6.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-109151
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 8:47 a.m. | 23 minutes ago
  
Description :In
the Matter and Aliro Door Lock Application of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door
Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1 with
CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE enabled, deleting a Credential Issuer passes the
1-based Matter credential index to ClearValidityIterations(), which expects a
0-based storage index. The intended issuer's ValidityIteration state is left in
place, and the state of the adjacent, still-provisioned issuer is cleared. This

been superseded, can then potentially obtain physical access. Fixed in v1.2.0.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-35190 - Out-of-Bounds Read in TLS 1.3 Key-Share Processing with Suite B Certificate Flag
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-35190
  
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 8:15 a.m. | 56 minutes ago
  
Description :Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B certificate flag through
SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read past the end of a
fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose supported_groups and
key_share contain no Suite B group.

Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello that makes the server
read past the end of a static array. The values read are never returned to the
client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with sanitizers or hardened
allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set, OpenSSL restricts the
accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed two-element list
for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used for key-share
selection was not updated for this substitution: tls1_get_group_tuples() still
returns the configured tuples, which by default describe eight groups. The
server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then advances through the
two-element list using those tuple counts without checking the cumulative
offset against the number of groups present.

Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with
SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are affected. The
openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509 verification parameter
instead, so the stock command line server is not vulnerable. Default
configurations do not reach this code.

A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set, such as X25519,
forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past the array. The bytes
read are compared against client group IDs and never sent back, so no memory
is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or hardened allocators the
read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it reads a few bytes of
adjacent constant data.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-93673 - WebSocket client accepts a handshake without verifying the full Sec-WebSocket-Accept value
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93673
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 5 minutes ago
  
Description :The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c. The comparison was performed as strncmp(at, str, length), where length is the length of the value the server sent rather than the length of the expected value, so the check only asked whether the received value was a prefix of the expected base64(SHA-1(key || GUID)). A server that returned a handful of correct characters passed, and a response carrying an empty Sec-WebSocket-Accept: header caused strncmp() to be called with a count of zero, which returns 0 and set ctx->sec_accept_ok with no comparison performed at all. The header-value callback also cleared ctx->sec_accept_present after the first chunk, so a value split across receive-buffer boundaries was only ever examined in part.

ctx->sec_accept_ok is the sole WebSocket-specific gate in websocket_connect(); the client does not check the HTTP status code or the Upgrade:/Connection: headers. Any HTTP response containing an empty or prefix-matching Sec-WebSocket-Accept header therefore completed the handshake, after which the socket is finalized as a WebSocket and all further peer bytes are parsed as frames. The affected path is driven directly by remote input through subsys/net/lib/http/http_parser.c, and is reached by every user of websocket_connect(), including MQTT over WebSocket (subsys/net/lib/mqtt/mqtt_transport_websocket.c) and subsys/net/lib/ocpp/ocpp.c.

The Sec-WebSocket-Accept exchange is not a secret-based authentication -- an endpoint or on-path attacker that sees the request can compute the expected value -- so the impact is bounded to parties that never observed the handshake request: a caching or transparent intermediary replaying a canned response, an off-path attacker injecting a spoofed response, or a non-WebSocket endpoint the client was induced to talk to. For those, the per-connection binding that RFC 6455 requires the client to enforce provided no protection at all, letting a single crafted response convince the device it holds a live WebSocket session and causing it to send application data to, and accept frames from, an unverified peer. There is no memory-safety consequence.

The fix compares each delivered chunk against the expected value at the position reached so far, refuses a chunk that would overrun it, and accepts only once every byte of the expected value -- and no more -- has been matched; on_header_field() now also clears the flag for any other header so a partial value cannot be continued across an intervening header.
  
Severity: 4.8 | MEDIUM

vulnerability.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93673
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 5 minutes ago
  
Description :The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c. The comparison was performed as strncmp(at, str, length), where length is the length of the value the server sent rather than the length of the expected value, so the check only asked whether the received value was a prefix of the expected base64(SHA-1(key || GUID)). A server that returned a handful of correct characters passed, and a response carrying an empty Sec-WebSocket-Accept: header caused strncmp() to be called with a count of zero, which returns 0 and set ctx->sec_accept_ok with no comparison performed at all. The header-value callback also cleared ctx->sec_accept_present after the first chunk, so a value split across receive-buffer boundaries was only ever examined in part.

ctx->sec_accept_ok is the sole WebSocket-specific gate in websocket_connect(); the client does not check the HTTP status code or the Upgrade:/Connection: headers. Any HTTP response containing an empty or prefix-matching Sec-WebSocket-Accept header therefore completed the handshake, after which the socket is finalized as a WebSocket and all further peer bytes are parsed as frames. The affected path is driven directly by remote input through subsys/net/lib/http/http_parser.c, and is reached by every user of websocket_connect(), including MQTT over WebSocket (subsys/net/lib/mqtt/mqtt_transport_websocket.c) and subsys/net/lib/ocpp/ocpp.c.

The Sec-WebSocket-Accept exchange is not a secret-based authentication -- an endpoint or on-path attacker that sees the request can compute the expected value -- so the impact is bounded to parties that never observed the handshake request: a caching or transparent intermediary replaying a canned response, an off-path attacker injecting a spoofed response, or a non-WebSocket endpoint the client was induced to talk to. For those, the per-connection binding that RFC 6455 requires the client to enforce provided no protection at all, letting a single crafted response convince the device it holds a live WebSocket session and causing it to send application data to, and accept frames from, an unverified peer. There is no memory-safety consequence.

The fix compares each delivered chunk against the expected value at the position reached so far, refuses a chunk that would overrun it, and accepts only once every byte of the expected value -- and no more -- has been matched; on_header_field() now also clears the flag for any other header so a partial value cannot be continued across an intervening header.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-93672 - NULL pointer dereference in the Bluetooth host ATT request lookup (bt_att_find_req_by_user_data)
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93672
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 5 minutes ago
  
Description :bt_att_find_req_by_user_data() in subsys/bluetooth/host/att.c walks every ATT channel attached to a connection and dereferences chan->req->user_data without checking chan->req. An ATT channel with no client request in flight holds chan->req == NULL — that is its normal idle state, set by att_handle_rsp() when a response resolves the transaction and tested by att_req_send_process() to pick a free channel — so the lookup reads through a NULL pointer as soon as it visits an idle channel. Every other chan->req user in the file already guards the pointer.

The lookup is reached from the public bt_gatt_cancel() API and, more importantly, from the host itself: bt_gatt_unsubscribe() calls bt_gatt_cancel() while a subscribe CCC write is still outstanding (BT_GATT_SUBSCRIBE_FLAG_WRITE_PENDING), and call_notify_cb_and_maybe_unsubscribe() in subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c invokes bt_gatt_unsubscribe() from the RX path whenever an application notify callback returns BT_GATT_ITER_STOP. A malicious or malfunctioning peer can hold the trigger window open by withholding the ATT Write Response to the CCC write and then sending a notification for the subscribed handle. With CONFIG_BT_EATT the traversal is very likely to meet an idle sibling channel, since ATT channels are prepended to the list and a channel opened after the pending request was sent is visited first.

The dereference is a read of a small constant offset from address zero, so the impact is availability only: no memory corruption, no attacker-chosen address and no information disclosure. On platforms and configurations where a near-NULL read traps — TrustZone non-secure images, MMU targets, native_sim, or builds with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_MPU/_DWT — the fault occurs in the Bluetooth RX context and results in a fatal error and device reset. On a plain Cortex-M build with the vector table mapped at address 0 and null-pointer detection disabled (the default) the read succeeds and the defect is inert.

The fix adds an explicit chan->req != NULL test to the channel traversal and additionally rejects a NULL user_data argument, which would otherwise have matched, and cancelled, an unrelated request.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-93666 - Bluetooth Classic SDP client can deadlock the Bluetooth workqueue on buffer allocation
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93666
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 5 minutes ago
  
Description :The Bluetooth Classic SDP client built its outgoing request PDUs with bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which allocates from the sdp_pool net-buf pool with a K_FOREVER timeout and no failure handling, in sdp_client_ss_search(), sdp_client_sa_search() and sdp_client_ssa_search() in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c. All of these run on the Bluetooth workqueue bt_workq (via sdp_client_work_handler(), the L2CAP sdp_client_connected() callback, or the continuation-state follow-up from a received response), which is the same single thread that dispatches incoming HCI ACL and event traffic, drives L2CAP, and performs connection and channel teardown. sdp_pool holds only CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN buffers (one by default) and is shared with the SDP server role.

An unauthenticated peer within BR/EDR range can drive both halves of the trigger. The SDP L2CAP server is registered at BT_SECURITY_L0, so any inbound SDP request makes the device allocate the pool's buffer for a response, which is held until the controller has transmitted it. The same peer can then cause a client request to be issued while the pool is empty: in-tree profiles start SDP discovery from inbound connection callbacks (for example hfp_hf_accept() calls bt_sdp_discover() through hfp_hf_create(), and hfp_ag.c mirrors this), and a peer acting as an SDP server can force repeated client requests by answering with partial responses carrying continuation state.

With the pool empty, the allocation blocks uninterruptibly and freezes the entire Bluetooth host. The stall becomes permanent when the release of the outstanding buffer itself depends on the blocked workqueue: if the link carrying the queued PDU is dropped or stalls, hci_disconn_complete() and the L2CAP channel cleanup that purges the channel TX queue are themselves bt_workq work items, so the buffer is never returned. The result is an unrecoverable denial of service of all Bluetooth functionality until reboot; there is no memory-safety, confidentiality or integrity impact.

The fix allocates client PDUs with K_NO_WAIT via a new sdp_client_create_pdu(), propagates -ENOBUFS, parks the session on a new SDP_CLIENT_FLAG_WAIT_FOR_TX_BUF flag, and adds an sdp_pool destructor that re-submits the SDP client worker when a buffer becomes available. Note that the SDP server role still allocated from the same pool with K_FOREVER at this commit; that path was addressed separately.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-69154 - Coder VS Code extension allowed workspace settings to trigger command execution
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-69154
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 1 hour, 58 minutes ago
  
Description :The Coder VS Code extension opens Coder workspaces in VS Code with a single click. From 0.1.20 until 1.14.6, a malicious repository can provide .vscode/settings.json values for security-sensitive Coder settings because the extension permits workspace and folder scope to override those settings. Values such as coder.headerCommand and coder.tlsCertRefreshCommand are later executed as shell commands, while other affected settings can redirect the Coder CLI binary or download source, inject CLI or SSH flags, replace TLS material, disable TLS verification, or change identity and credential-storage behavior. A victim with the extension installed must open the malicious workspace or repository; when the extension activates, attacker-controlled commands can run with the victim user's privileges. The issue also affects untrusted workspaces because the extension declares untrusted-workspace support without preventing consumption of the workspace-controlled settings. This issue is fixed in version 1.14.6.

Description :Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, ContentPreprocessor.preprocess() in guard_core/detection_engine/preprocessor.py collapses all whitespace before built-in pattern matching in the default enhanced mode. The affected dynamic route must have a prerenderable param declared by generateStaticParams whose requested value was not generated at build time, at least two never-prerenderable params below it, a layout that reads the shallower param inside a Suspense boundary, and a blocking fallback shell. vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129306

Description :libspdm is a sample implementation that follows the DMTF SPDM specifications. Prior to 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2, libspdm_x509_verify_cert_chain() in os_stub/cryptlib_openssl/pk/x509.c and os_stub/cryptlib_mbedtls/pk/x509.c validates certificate signatures one link at a time instead of validating the complete X.509 path. In deployments using a pinned root with a constrained multi-tier PKI, an attacker holding a valid issuer credential below a constrained CA can present a subordinate certificate that exceeds pathLenConstraint or nameConstraints and may be accepted for SPDM identity validation. vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-129237 - qbee-agent: Docker Compose build context Zip Slip writes outside context directory
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129237
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 4:52 p.m. | 9 minutes ago
  
Description :qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.41, the unpackTar extraction logic in app/utils/tar.go validates cleaned archive entry paths with strings.HasPrefix(targetPath, destdirClean) without enforcing a path-separator boundary. When UseContext enables the Docker Compose build context path in app/configuration/bundle_docker_compose.go, a less-privileged archive supplier with delegated configuration and/or file-manager access can provide a sibling-prefix traversal entry that passes the check, causing utils.UnpackTar to create directories and regular files outside the intended context extraction directory with qbee-agent process privileges, despite the supplier lacking authority to write those sibling files. In deployments where only full device or fleet administrators can provide Docker Compose context archives, this behavior is hardening rather than a crossed security boundary. The demonstrated impact is limited to nearby cache or project paths sharing the destination prefix, may affect integrity or availability of qbee-agent-managed Docker Compose state, and does not establish arbitrary absolute-path writes or direct code execution. This issue is fixed in version 2026.41.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-129919 - Kunai Mount Namespace Cache TOCTOU Allows Incorrect Event Resolution Against Host Files
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129919
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 1:49 p.m. | 34 minutes ago
  
Description :Kunai, a security monitoring tool, contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in its mount namespace (mnt ns) caching logic. When resolving a security event that references a specific process PID and an expected mount namespace, the Switcher::new function read /proc//ns/mnt to determine the target namespace and cached the result under the expected namespace key without verifying that the resolved namespace actually matched the expected one.

An attacker with local access could exploit this by either (1) arranging for the referenced PID to be reused by a process in a different namespace (e.g., the host namespace) before Kunai resolves it, or (2) calling unshare or setns on the target process after the event is generated but before the namespace is resolved. In either case, the wrong namespace (potentially the host's own namespace) would be cached under the container's namespace key.

The security impact is that subsequent container security events would be resolved against host filesystem paths rather than container paths. This undermines the integrity of the security monitoring data: container activity could be misattributed to the host, host activity could be misattributed to a container, and file-path-based detections or alerts would reference incorrect paths. An attacker could potentially use this to obscure malicious activity within a container by making it appear as benign host activity, or to generate misleading security alerts.

The vulnerability requires local access to the system and a specific timing window between event generation and namespace resolution. No remote attack vector or user interaction is required.
  
Severity: 2.0 | LOW
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-110710 - @fastify/multipart vulnerable to Denial of Service via temporary file leak after client disconnect
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-110710
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 1:17 p.m. | 17 minutes ago
  
Description :@fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 3.0.0 through 10.1.3, temporary files written by the saveRequestFiles helper are removed only by a response hook that runs when the response finishes or errors. When a client completes an upload and then disconnects before the handler writes the reply, for example while the handler scans, hashes or forwards the file, the response only emits a close event, the cleanup hook never runs, and the saved files are left on disk. An unauthenticated client can repeat this cheaply to exhaust disk space and deny service to applications that save uploaded files to disk. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.4, and users should upgrade to 10.1.4 or later. As a workaround, avoid saving request files for untrusted clients, or clean the saved files from a close handler on the raw response so removal also happens when the client disconnects.
  
Severity: 7.5 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-129784 - Insecure deserializaiton in the httpx Ruby gem via unsafe Oj object-mode
vulnerability.summary:

Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:53 a.m. | 9 minutes ago
  
Description :The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99308 - usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99308
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:17 a.m. | 45 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow

High-speed devices with out of spec 1024 byte bulk endpoints exist and
are allowed by USB core, but xhci-hcd always sets packet size to 512.
The exact nature of these devices isn't documented, commit fb5ee84ea72c
("USB: Accept bulk endpoints with 1024-byte maxpacket") only states
that they "don't work with xHCI host controllers", whatever it means.

But somebody (or a malicious device) can try, and then the driver will
allocate a 512 byte bounce buffer for this endpoint and may write up to
1024 bytes into it if particular scatter-gather URBs are used, because
xhci_align_td() obtains packet size from the descriptor. Fix this.

As a side effect, TRBs will be aligned to the packet size chosen by the
driver on all endpoints of all speeds. Alignment serves the xHC, not
device, so this is fine. Only out of spec devices are affected anyway.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99311 - udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99311
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 9:59 a.m. | 24 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()

When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains
other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash
like:

 Oops: general protection fault
 KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access
 RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503)
 Call Trace:
  vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419)
  do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583)
  __x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602)

This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return
value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through
udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being
treated as a folio pointer with obvious results.

Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either
0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease

parse_reply_info_lease() reads a 32-bit struct_len off the wire and only

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99292 - smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99292
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 9:59 a.m. | 24 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()

In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after
commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group
rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or
5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace)
on posix).

However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() ->
copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total),
and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes)
even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security
descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or
dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past
the end of the slab buffer.

Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of
id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99290 - ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99290
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 9:59 a.m. | 24 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect

ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the
reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry.
If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to
remove the volatile id.

Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before
either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops
its references first, the other request makes the final put through
ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first
session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed
memory.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
  Call Trace:
   __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 1030:
   __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd]

Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file
lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not
one made by another holder.

Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path,
before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the
request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which
holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup
is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-115690 - Apache WSS4J: Replay protection bypassed by concurrent copies of a message
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-115690
  
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 9:54 a.m. | 29 minutes ago
  
Description :Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice. It checked whether a value had already been seen, validated the message, and only then remembered the value, as two separate steps. If several copies of the same message were processed at the same time, they could all pass the check before any of them was remembered, and all be accepted. An attacker who obtained a valid message before the recipient first processed it could send several copies at once, so that the same authenticated request was executed more than once. Where a UsernameToken is not bound to the message by a signature, the copies could carry different message bodies. The attacker needs to obtain the message while it is still in transit; a message captured after it has been accepted cannot be replayed. Affects deployments with a replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by default. The value is now checked and remembered in a single atomic step. Custom ReplayCache implementations should override the new ReplayCache.addIfAbsent method with an operation that is atomic in their underlying store. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.3 or 3.0.7 or 2.4.5, which fix this issue.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-123638 - Gitea protected file pattern bypass with quoted file names
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-123638
  
Published : Nov. 15, 2026, 9:14 p.m. | 44 minutes ago
  
Description :The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path.
